clue.text: Biscuits and nuts

definitions.meaning: dry savoury biscuits, often eaten with cheese
informal word for mad or crazy

explanation.definitionFit: Savoury wafers eaten with cheese go by this name, and the same word is slang for insane.

clue.text: Two characters from Athens full of new wheezes

indicators.note: the two Greek letters together are filled with the abbreviation for new

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the alphabet of Athens
chi is another Greek letter

explanation.surface: A pair of Athenians are full of fresh comic schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' is the container signal. 'Wheezes' looks like jokes or schemes in the surface, but here it is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhonchi are the rattling, whistling sounds heard in the chest when airways are narrowed, a medical term for wheezing noises.

clue.text: Car with just two doors two left out

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the word for a pair

parts.note: a couple is a pair, two of something

explanation.surface: A two-door car, with a couple left outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes L from COUPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupé is a body style of motor car with a fixed roof and only two doors.

clue.text: He catches salesman and wife, taken up short

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the whole run is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: short means the word for a spouse loses its final letter

parts.note: a wife is a partner in marriage

explanation.surface: A salesman and his wife, taken up short by a fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops a final letter and 'taken up' reverses everything, which suits a down entry read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sets a snare or trick to catch somebody is an ensnarer, and the clue's pronoun stands for that person.

clue.text: Presume to order the best

indicators.note: putting letters to order means arranging them afresh, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone presumes to give orders to the finest people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to order' rearranges the letters of PRESUME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supreme is the highest or finest of all, as in a supreme champion.

clue.text: Jolly Jack and I'll be in sports ground

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: I will be in means the letter I goes inside the word for the ground

parts.note: an oval is a sports ground, as in the Oval cricket ground in London
I'll is I will, so the letter I

explanation.surface: Cheerful Jack says he will be at the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'll be in' as 'I will be in': 'be in' puts I inside OVAL. THE OVAL is a famous London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial and jolly are synonyms, both describing someone cheerful and good-humoured.

clue.text: Someone younger's right for most of Ulster — he swears in company

indicators.note: right taking the place of most of Ulster is a swap of one bit for another

parts.note: a junior is someone younger; the 's is 'has'
Northern Ireland (NI) covers six of Ulster's nine counties, so it is most of Ulster

explanation.surface: A younger person from Ulster swears loyalty in company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps NI out of JUNIOR and puts R in its place. Ulster is the historic Irish province of nine counties; six of them form Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a jury takes an oath and sits with eleven others, so this person swears in company.

clue.text: Putting on coat, run off making an exit

indicators.note: off means the letter for run is taken away

parts.note: varnishing is putting on a coat of varnish
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone putting on a coat runs off and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes R from VARNISHING. 'Coat' suggests clothing, but it is a coat of varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappearing from view is a way of leaving, as in a vanishing act.

clue.text: Brief defence in court and US lawyers he wasn't part of the criminal gang

definitions.text: he wasn't part of the criminal gang

indicators.note: brief means the defence word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an alibi is a defence claiming to be elsewhere at the time of a crime
the ABA is the American Bar Association

explanation.surface: A short defence in court and American lawyers fail to show he was not in the gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' cuts ALIBI to ALIB. 'Brief' also suggests a barrister, which is a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale the woodcutter discovers the cave of the Forty Thieves but is not one of them.

clue.text: Beefy's shattered following run out

indicators.note: following means the word for shattered comes after the cricket abbreviation

parts.note: RO is the cricket abbreviation for run out
bust means broken or shattered

explanation.surface: Ian Botham, nicknamed Beefy, is exhausted after being run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefy is the nickname of the English cricketer Ian Botham, which makes the cricket surface; here it is just an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy and robust both describe someone strong, sturdy and well built.

clue.text: Strike back at one upsetting by rumour — when in such a state?

indicators.note: back means the word for strike is read in reverse

parts.note: to rap is to strike

indicators.note: by rumour means what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an annoyer is one who upsets people

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by gossip and lashes out in return, as if they were persecuted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAP into PAR; 'by rumour' says ANNOYER is taken as it sounds, giving ANOIA. The question mark marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Paranoia is a mental condition of unfounded suspicion, the very state of someone who thinks rumours are aimed at them.

clue.text: Maze for redesigning following community's complaint

indicators.note: following means the rearranged letters come after the community abbreviation

parts.note: EC is the European Community

indicators.note: something up for redesigning is to be reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A maze is redesigned to suit a local community's complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance in the surface, but it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and this skin inflammation is one such ailment.

clue.text: Area is united from constituent parts

definitions.text: Area is united from constituent parts

indicators.note: made from constituent parts means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A region is formed by joining its constituent parts together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from constituent parts' rearranges AREA IS plus U. The whole clue also describes the landmass: Europe and Asia joined.
explanation.definitionFit: The combined landmass of Europe and Asia is one area made of two continents.

clue.text: Bit of mistletoe, popular piece when drunk — a feature of Xmas parties

indicators.note: a bit of the plant here means only its first letter

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Kissing under the mistletoe and getting drunk are features of Christmas parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' takes M from mistletoe; 'when drunk' rearranges PIECE into CEPIE.
explanation.definitionFit: These small pastries filled with dried fruit are traditional festive fare served at Christmas gatherings.

clue.text: Perhaps Black Lace sing badly?

parts.note: to chant is to sing
illy is an old-fashioned word for badly

explanation.surface: Did the pop group Black Lace sing badly?
explanation.walkthrough: Black Lace were a British pop group known for novelty hits like 'Agadoo', so the surface teases their singing. 'Perhaps' says black lace is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantilly is a fine bobbin lace, traditionally made in black silk, so black lace is one example.

clue.text: First of clues by Raich foxed an old president

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of clues
foxed means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A solver is baffled by clues from a setter called Raich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' takes C; 'foxed' rearranges RAICH into HIRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Chirac was the French head of state from 1995 to 2007.

clue.text: Blades? Bet others caught by riot gas

indicators.note: caught by means the betting words are held inside the gas

parts.note: CS gas is used for riot control
to lay is to bet
more means additional ones, others

explanation.surface: Gamblers are caught by tear gas thrown at a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' is the container signal; CS gas is a riot-control tear gas. The question mark shows the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large Scottish broadsword, a kind of weapon with a long steel edge.

clue.text: Returning empty animal tucked into cereal cake

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembled run is read backwards
tucked into means one bit goes inside the cereal word

parts.note: rice is a cereal crop

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the animal word is taken out, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A hungry animal is tucked into its cereal and a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves AL from animal; 'tucked into' puts it in RICE, making RIALCE, and 'Returning' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream, a type of small cake.

clue.text: This could be so nice with a drop of liqueur nearby

indicators.note: this could be says the answer is a rearrangement of the words that follow
a drop of means just the first letter of liqueur

explanation.surface: A drop of liqueur could make something quite pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a drop of' gives L; 'This could be' rearranges SO NICE plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Close-in means near at hand, in the immediate vicinity.

clue.text: Peal provided by family group — that's good of us

parts.note: a clan is a family group
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A family group rings bells together, which is kind of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is a loud ringing or clanging noise, such as a peal of bells.

clue.text: Like some cream over the top? Crown of 14 went first round the sides

indicators.note: the crown is the top, and in a down clue the top of 14 is its first letter

parts.note: the number points to the answer at 14-down, the lace

indicators.note: round the sides means the word for went first wraps around the other piece

parts.note: led means went first

explanation.surface: Is cream on top of Chantilly a bit excessive?
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 points to the answer at 14-down, whose top letter is C. 'round the sides' is the container signal; 'over the top?' reads as part of the cream picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick clotted cream, made by heating milk slowly, is a West Country speciality served with scones.

clue.text: Rustles tailored coats

indicators.note: tailored means altered, so these letters are recut

explanation.surface: A tailor rustles up some coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' rearranges RUSTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose overcoat, so coats of this style share the name.

clue.text: When in capital, briefly on train transported between outskirts of Oslo

indicators.note: between means the rearranged train is placed inside the outer letters
outskirts of means just the first and last letters of Oslo
transported means moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In a capital city, someone takes a quick ride on a train through the outskirts of Oslo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges TRAIN into NTARI, and 'between' puts it inside O and O. In Toronto, the provincial capital, the province is abbreviated ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Its capital is Toronto and its postal abbreviation is ON, so in its capital you are briefly in ON.

clue.text: You have to thread a way through here eventually

definitions.text: You have to thread a way

indicators.note: through means the answer runs within the next words

explanation.surface: Eventually you have to find a way through here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' hides the answer in 'heRE EVEntually'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reeve is a nautical verb meaning to pass a rope through a hole or block.

clue.text: Characterless type eating seconds for pudding?

indicators.note: eating means the word for the timid person swallows the letter for seconds

parts.note: a mouse is a timid, characterless person

explanation.surface: A dull person tucks into seconds of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts S inside MOUSE. The question mark allows a light, airy dessert as a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousse is a light, airy dessert of whipped cream or egg white, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Machinegun duel — to some extent that's not called for

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A machine-gun duel is excessive to some extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' hides the answer in 'machinegUN DUEl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwarranted or excessive is unnecessary, more than the situation demands.

clue.text: Becoming 'run down' from Spanish influenza's a medical specialism

parts.note: de is the Spanish word for from
flu is short for influenza
ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: Feeling run down after Spanish flu has become a medical specialism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run down' suggests tired, but here it means flowing downwards; 'Becoming' signals the sense of moving into that state.
explanation.definitionFit: Defluent is a rare adjective for something flowing or running downward.

clue.text: What shows you're dreaming about a letter for ransom?

indicators.note: about means the sleep phase abbreviation goes around the letter

parts.note: REM, rapid eye movement, is the sleep phase when dreams occur
dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

explanation.surface: Is dreaming about a letter demanding a ransom a sign of something?
explanation.walkthrough: REM sleep (rapid eye movement) is the phase when dreams happen; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransom a captive is to buy them back, which is what redeeming means.

clue.text: Vital agent Z infiltrating enemy ground

indicators.note: infiltrating means Z gets inside the rearranged letters
ground means crushed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Agent Z infiltrates enemy territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges ENEMY into ENYME, and 'infiltrating' puts Z inside. 'Ground' looks like territory but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: These proteins act as catalysts essential to the chemistry of life, so each is a vital agent.

clue.text: Pluto essentially is going to melt away

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, identified with Pluto
per se means essentially, by itself

explanation.surface: Pluto is essentially going to vanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluto' looks like the dwarf planet, but it is the god of the underworld, called Dis by the Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter and vanish, like a crowd or mist dissolving.
